title: Cost-threshold safety layer with prefetch checkpoints and state-merge rollback
creator: Alex Kim
description: Goal: Implement an automatic rollback safety layer that uses economic and correctness signals to safely revert risky config changes while preserving runtime state (KV cache, batching heuristics) where possible. This work combines: (1) pre-apply checkpointing of serving state, (2) lightweight preflight and shadow simulations, (3) multi-signal rollback triggers (cost threshold, token-quality regressions, latency SLO violations), and (4) deterministic state-merge reconciliation for KV caches to avoid cold-cache penalties after revert. The design prioritizes minimal customer-visible disruption and cost-sensitive hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping during noise.

acceptance_criteria: Can create a pre-apply checkpoint that captures KV cache deltas and batching pointers within 500ms for typical pool sizes
Preflight simulation runs in under 2s for small config diffs and returns a deterministic cost_delta estimate
Rollback triggers evaluate combined signal: 1) cost_delta > configurable threshold, 2) latency breach > SLO window, or 3) token-quality regression > configured tolerance
Hysteresis: requires either sustained signal for 3 consecutive windows or cross-signal agreement to trigger automatic rollback
State-merge reconciler can rehydrate compatible KV entries from checkpoint into the reverted instance without corrupting per-request routing
End-to-end test: injected cost spike during canary causes safe revert and preserves >80% of hot-KV hits after revert compared to baseline
Metrics and runbook entries added to Console and runbook links available in ticket
Feature flag gating implemented for per-team enablement and enterprise opt-out
